chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Work and recording dates in New York with Vinson
summary: He recalls his first New York record date and says Vinson's was a good band; he first met Krupa when with Basie.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah. So here you were working with Cleanhead, but as you recorded with different people.
Oh, sure, that's right.
Yeah.
I was doing that. And I'm trying to think of my very first recording date in New York. It was at the Capitol Studio.
Yeah.
And it was -- I think it was -- it was, it was Billie Holiday, I believe.
Was it?
My side date. Billie Holiday, and also the Ink Spots.
Oh, yeah, yeah. Listen, Gus, that wasn't Gus Arnheim you were thinking of, was it?
No, no.
Yeah. It wasn't Russ that played the trombone.
No. Russ Colombo?
Yeah.
No.
No? Okay, never mind. Well, so that was good. So -- but then, you enjoyed it with Cleanhead.
Oh, yes, sure.
That was a good band.
It was a good band, very good band.
And it must be nice to be playing in New York, but have everybody listening to you. You know what I mean.
Oh, sure.
Coming up to hear the band, and --
We did a lot of tours.
Did Krupa used to come up and listen to you at all?
He might have. First time I met Krupa, I was with Basie.
Oh.
And that was in Atlantic City.
Oh, yeah. Well, he had his own band and everything.
Oh, yes, he had his own band.
Yeah.
But he came by to hear Basie.
Yeah, yeah.
It was the Paradise Club.
Yeah.
That's another story.
